title: Make the page-size warnings say what the client sent

blocks.text: The orders endpoint pages its results, and a client may ask for its own page size with the `pageSize` query parameter. Support keeps getting tickets that read "my page size is ignored", and the warnings the endpoint records don't help: they should show what the client sent, and they should only appear when the client sent something unusable.
`Pagination` already pages correctly once it knows the size. Finish `pageSizeFor(...)` in `src/main/java/practice/Pagination.java`:

items: an `Integer` from 1 to `MAX_PAGE_SIZE` is used as it is;
with no `pageSize` at all, the endpoint's default is used and nothing is recorded;
anything else gets the default too, and one warning that shows the value the client sent.

cases.says: a pageSize the endpoint can use decides the size of the page
a request without a pageSize gets the endpoint's default
zero, a size over the limit, a string and a Long all get the endpoint's default
the warning for an unusable pageSize names the value the client sent, not the endpoint's default
a request that sends no pageSize at all records no warning

origin.section: Out of Its Scope, a Pattern Variable's Name Means the Field

concepts: Where a pattern variable is out of scope, a field of the same name is used without any error, so a guard that falls through reads the field.
